chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us; he said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sukri narrated to us; he said: Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Juwhari narrated to us; he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ammara narrated to us, from his father, who said: The Truthful (Al-Sadiq), Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), said:

The four things people seek in this ephemeral world are: wealth, comfort, lack of concern, and honor. As for wealth, it is found in contentment; whoever seeks it in the abundance of money will not find it. As for comfort, it is found in a light burden; whoever seeks it in a heavy burden will not find it. As for lack of concern, it is found in little busyness; whoever seeks it amidst much busyness will not find it. As for honor, it is found in serving the Creator; whoever seeks it in serving the creation will not find it.
ai.seo_question: What are the four things people seek in this world and how does Imam al-Sadiq define their true essence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) redefines the four worldly pursuits—wealth, comfort, peace of mind, and honor—by shifting the focus from external accumulation to internal spiritual states. He teaches that true wealth is found in contentment (*qana'ah*), comfort in a light burden, peace in minimal distraction, and honor in serving the Creator rather than created beings. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not as poverty, but as a state of heart detached from materialism while remaining engaged in divine service.
